extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX users creating diagrams with TikZ (authors of technical/math diagrams)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and options for placing nodes, labels, pins, shapes, and matrices in TikZ pictures; covers node placement semantics, shape spacing, remembering pictures across environments, and matrix alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: allow upside down
rubrics_metrics.description: allow upside down=(true|false) — If set to true, TikZ will not “righten” upside down text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally rotation is done so text is not upside down. To intentionally get upside-down text use [rotate=180] or set allow upside down=true (or use the allow upside down key in a scope/picture).

rubrics_metrics.name: style positions (midway, near start, near end, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Predefined position styles map to pos values: style=midway → pos=0.5; near start → pos=0.25; near end → pos=0.75; very near start → pos=0.125; very near end → pos=0.875; at start → pos=0; at end → pos=1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provide less technical ways to specify node placement along a path (line or curve). Use the style names in option lists or set pos explicitly for fine control.

rubrics_metrics.name: implicit node placement on a line or curve
rubrics_metrics.description: When a node is specified inside a line/curve operation (e.g., (0,0) -- node{a} (1,1)), TikZ stores the node specification and inserts it after the final coordinate with pos set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: (1) Catcodes of stored node specs are fixed, so avoid complicated verbatim material — put such text in a following normal node with pos. (2) pos is inherited from surrounding scope only for nodes specified implicitly inside the path operation; adding [near end] to a scope does not affect explicitly placed nodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: label option syntax and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: label=[options](angle):(text) — Adds an extra node (label node) placed relative to the main node: the label node's anchor is placed at main node.<angle> (angle may be numeric or keywords like left/right/above).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can pass options to the label node by writing them in square brackets before the angle (use braces around the whole label arg if it contains brackets/commas). Multiple label options create multiple labels in the given order. Styles affecting labels: label distance (default 0pt) and style=every label (default draw=none,fill=none).

rubrics_metrics.name: pin option (labels with edges)
rubrics_metrics.description: pin=[options](angle):(text) — Like label but also draws an edge from the pin node to the main node (creates a pin appearance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pin-specific styles: pin distance (distance between main and pin node; default 3ex), style=every pin (default draw=none,fill=none), style=every pin edge (default help lines), and pin edge=options to style the connecting edge. You can customize pin edges (e.g., arrows, snake=snake) or set every pin edge globally.

rubrics_metrics.name: using nodes as coordinates (anchors vs center vs border behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description:
Once a node is defined (e.g., 
ode(x){...};) you can use (x.anchor) to get the anchor position (not affected by transformations) or use (x) which usually behaves like (x.center) but path operations like -- will shorten lines to the border of the node in the direction of the other endpoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transforms (scale/rotate) do not affect (x.anchor) coordinates. For shape=coordinate nodes, (x) equals (x.center) and line-shortening rules do not apply — useful when you need coordinates without shortening/segmentation (e.g., to allow filling).

rubrics_metrics.name: edge operation semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: \path ... edge[options] (nodes) (coordinate) ... ; — The edge operation suspends the main path and constructs a new path p drawn after the main path. The new path's start is \tikztostart (the last coordinate before the edge), with one exception: if edge directly follows a node operation, start is the just-declared node (not its placed coordinate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple edge operations in a row share the same start coordinate (the coordinate before the first edge). Edge paths inherit options from the main path but can locally override them. This allows different appearances per-edge. The style every edge is installed at the beginning of the main path (default: drawn).

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every edge / every to
rubrics_metrics.description: Styles every edge (and every to) allow setting defaults for edges/to operations on the main path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \tikzstyle{every to}=[draw,dashed] makes all to operations draw dashed lines. Use these to globally control appearance of edges added by edge/to operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: remember picture (referencing nodes across pictures)
rubrics_metrics.description: remember picture=(true|false) — Tells TikZ to attempt to remember the position of the current picture on the page so it can be referenced later (from other pictures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To reference nodes in different pictures, add remember picture to all pictures that define or reference such nodes. Remembering may depend on driver support (currently pdfTeX) and may require running TeX twice. You can set \tikzstyle{every picture}+=[remember picture] to enable remembering globally (writes lines to .aux).

rubrics_metrics.name: overlay option (cross-picture references and bounding box)
rubrics_metrics.description: overlay — When used on a picture or path, its contents are not taken into consideration when computing the bounding box of the current picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use overlay on all paths/pictures that reference nodes in other pictures; otherwise TikZ will expand the current picture to encompass remote nodes and repeated runs can blow up the size. Typically specify overlay for any picture drawing lines to nodes in other pictures.

rubrics_metrics.name: driver and run requirements for remembered pictures
rubrics_metrics.description: Referencing nodes in other pictures requires a driver that supports picture remembering (pdfTeX) and typically requires running TeX twice for positions to be available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If picture remembering does not seem to work, check driver support and run TeX twice. The manual recommends pdfTeX for this feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: current page node for absolute positioning
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a special node current page (shape rectangle) whose south west is the lower-left page corner and north east is the upper-right corner; can be referenced as if defined in a remembered picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By using remember picture and overlay you can position nodes absolutely on the page relative to (current page.*) anchors (e.g., placing text in corners or centered watermark text). Examples include placing a node at (current page.center) or (current page.south west) with shifts and style options.

rubrics_metrics.name: predefined shapes (rectangle, circle, coordinate) and libraries
rubrics_metrics.description: By default pgf/TikZ defines shapes: rectangle, circle, and coordinate. Additional shapes (ellipse, diamond, transistor, etc.) are available via libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different shapes have shape-specific behavior. Many common options (inner/outer sep, minimum size, aspect) apply to most shapes, but special-purpose shapes may expose additional options.

rubrics_metrics.name: inner sep / inner xsep / inner ysep
rubrics_metrics.description: inner sep=(dimension) adds invisible separation inside the shape between the text and the shape’s background path (acts like padding). inner xsep/ysep specify the separation only in x/y direction. Default inner sep equals a normal space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use inner sep to control padding; examples show inner sep=0pt for tight boxes and larger values for looser text placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: outer sep / outer xsep / outer ysep
rubrics_metrics.description: outer sep=(dimension) adds invisible space outside the background path, moving anchors outward. outer xsep/ysep specify only x/y directions. Default is half the line width.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When shape is filled but not drawn, default outer sep may be undesirable — set outer sep=0pt in that case. Outer sep affects where anchors lie relative to drawn background paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: minimum height / minimum width / minimum size / aspect
rubrics_metrics.description: minimum height/width=(dimension) ensure the shape's dimension is at least the given size (including inner sep). minimum size sets both height and width. aspect=(ratio) sets desired aspect ratio for certain shapes (e.g., diamond width:height).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These options enlarge shapes when text+inner sep is smaller than desired but do not shrink shapes if text is larger. Use to create consistent node sizes or square/circular nodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: coordinate shape special handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Nodes with shape=coordinate are handled specially: using (x) as a coordinate equals (x.center), and line-shortening rules do not apply; paths remain unsegmented so can be filled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use coordinate shape when you need a purely positional node without affecting path shortening/filling behavior (e.g., creating polygon fills between coordinates).

rubrics_metrics.name: after node path option (execute path after node)
rubrics_metrics.description: after node path=(path) — Adds the given path to the main path right after the node as if given immediately after; can only be given inside a node option list. Multiple uses accumulate. Within the path \tikzlastnode references the node just created.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is useful for styles that need to add decorations relative to the node (e.g., drawing a circle around the node). Note: if you use \path instead of \draw for the main path, the added path may not be drawn because it's part of the main path rather than the node.

rubrics_metrics.name: \tikzaddafternodepathoption (prepending code to after node path)
rubrics_metrics.description: \tikzaddafternodepathoption{code} — Specifies code to be executed at the beginning of the after node path of the current node; code executes immediately and again at the beginning of any after node path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this command to ensure certain node-after behavior is prepended consistently; useful for package or style authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: matrices are nodes (matrix option and \matrix abbreviation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Matrices are implemented as nodes: node[matrix] (matrix=true by default). Inside tikzpicture the shorthand \matrix is equivalent to \path node[matrix].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because matrices are nodes they can have shapes, anchors, and be drawn/filled like nodes. However, some node options behave differently for matrices: rotations and scaling have no effect on the matrix as a whole (the rotational/scaling part of the transformation matrix is reset before typesetting the matrix), and options starting with text (e.g., text width) do not apply to the matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: matrix cell pictures: \ (end row) and & (cell separator)
rubrics_metrics.description: A matrix consists of rows of cell pictures. Each row (including the last) must be ended with \\. The character & separates cells. Cell pictures are drawing commands (not full pgfpicture envs) and empty cells are auto-added if rows have differing lengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to end the last row with \\ leads to incorrect matrix formation. Cell pictures cannot use layers. Treat each cell as a small picture: put nodes/draw commands inside cells.

rubrics_metrics.name: matrix alignment rules for rows and columns
rubrics_metrics.description: Row alignment: for a row, cell picture origins are shifted to lie on the same horizontal line; the row's top is the highest bounding-box top, bottom is lowest bounding-box bottom. Rows are stacked so bottom of previous touches top of next (unless row sep used). Column alignment: cell origins aligned on a vertical line; column left/right determined by extreme bounding boxes and columns abut unless column sep used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each row/column typically has its own computed height/depth/width. Understanding origin alignment is important for positioning content inside cells and for predictable layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: column sep spacing list semantics (including between origins/between borders)
rubrics_metrics.description: column sep=(spacing list) sets default spacing added between every two columns; the spacing list may contain numbers and keywords between origins or between borders. Numbers are summed. The last occurrence of the keywords determines behavior: between borders (or none) inserts space between column borders; between origins adjusts columns so distance between cell origins equals the given distance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The between origins option can only be used for columns mentioned in the first row (cannot be specified for columns introduced later). column sep may be a single dimension or a list with mixed entries for fine control.

rubrics_metrics.name: row sep spacing list and \\ optional dimension argument
rubrics_metrics.description: row sep=(spacing list) works like column sep but for rows, with the same between origins/between borders behavior. The \ command accepts an optional dimension argument which is added to row sep for that specific row pair and may include between origins/between borders to locally override defaults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the \[dim,between origins] (or between borders) form to vary spacing for individual row separations. The optional argument affects only the pair being ended by that \\.

rubrics_metrics.name: & optional spacing list (per-column adjustments)
rubrics_metrics.description: The & cell separator optionally takes a spacing list which is added to the global column sep. This optional spacing list only has effect the first time a new column is started (usually in the first row); later uses of & in that column do not change the column separation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the &[...] form in the first row to set per-column spacing (e.g., & [2mm] to add 2mm to that column separation). This is analogous to \ optional argument for rows.

rubrics_metrics.name: cell styles and node defaults inside matrices
rubrics_metrics.description: style=every cell is executed at the beginning of each cell picture (but setting draw there won't auto-draw nodes unless draw is passed to each node). cells=options adds options to every cell (shorthand), nodes=options adds options to every node inside the matrix (shorthand).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Row/column/cell-specific styles: style=column<number>, style=every odd column, style=every even column, style=row<number>, style=every odd row, style=every even row, and style=row<row number> column<column number> allow targeted styling. Inside cell styles the counters \pgfmatrixcurrentrow and \pgfmatrixcurrentcolumn are available.
